source.author: stat
source.text: Tertius horrentem zephyris laxaverat annum Phoebus et angustum cogebat limite verno longius ire diem, eum fracta impulsaque fatis consilia et tandem miseri data copia belli, prima manu rutilam de vertice Larissaco ostendit Bellona facem dextraque trabalem hastam intorsit agens, liquido quae stridula caelo fugit et Aoniae celso stetit aggere Dirces.
source.text_original: Tertius horrentem zephyris laxaverat annum / Phoebus et angustum cogebat limite verno / longius ire diem, eum fracta impulsaque fatis / consilia et tandem miseri data copia belli, / prima manu rutilam de vertice Larissaco / ostendit Bellona facem dextraque trabalem / hastam intorsit agens, liquido quae stridula caelo / fugit et Aoniae celso stetit aggere Dirces.
source.text_english: Phoebus had already loosened the third year with the west winds, and was compelling the day, still short, to go farther along its spring path, when, plans broken and driven by fate and at last opportunity given for wretched war, Bellona first showed her ruddy torch from the Larissan summit with her right hand, and with her right hand hurled the beam-like spear, driving it on, which hissed as it sped through the clear sky and came to rest on the high embankment of Aonian Dirce.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_original: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis / fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras / ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus / rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_english: First we sing of the sea passages made traversable by the great sons of the gods, and of the prophetic ship, which, daring to follow the Scythian shores of Phasis and, driven on, to break through its course amid the middle mountain ridges, at last settled on fiery Olympus.
